Name: The Funeral Origins of Gladiatorial Games and the Tradition of Blood Offerings to the Dead
RagShortTexts: Roman gladiatorial combat originated in the funeral combat rites of Campanian and Etruscan nobles
Before the cremation pyre of a distinguished noble killed in war, captives and slaves were made to duel so that their blood would appease the departed spirit
In 216 BC the funeral of Marcus Aemilius first featured dozens of pairs of gladiators fighting over three days
BaseText: The Roman gladiatorial games familiar to modern people were, in the time of the Second Punic War, not simple popular entertainment but a sacred and grim funeral rite, the 'Munera' (meaning the final duty offered to the dead). The custom came from ancient Etruscan and Campanian beliefs; the early Romans firmly believed that the shades of fallen noble heroes had to drink the hot blood shed by captive warriors in order to rest in the underworld and not become vengeful ghosts haunting the living. In 216 BC, after the Battle of Cannae, the former consul and pontifex Marcus Aemilius Lepidus died, and his three sons held funeral games in the Forum Boarium for three consecutive days, driving twenty-two pairs of fully armed Samnite captives to fight to the death with short swords. Their blood soaked the earth of the forum, and it marked the beginning of Rome's use of gladiatorial blood offerings in a time of national mourning and crisis to bind together the martial spirit of its citizens.

Variants.Content: This is the most solemn offering to noble spirits! Let the captives stab at one another before my late father's shade; only when the cremation pyre is soaked in blood can the souls of our ancestors protect the Republic from the underworld!

We were captured at Cannae. We did not die before the spear line, but were pushed onto the sand pit as offerings and forced to draw our swords against brothers who were captured with us. Roman savagery is crueler than the beasts of the wilderness!

Watching the sparks fly where short swords clash on the sand and smelling hot blood, the whole city roars! In this war there is only death in battle, and whoever retreats is lower than the corpses in the pit!
